title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ecclesiastes chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ecclesiastes Chapter 1.

questions.question: Who is described as the Preacher in Ecclesiastes chapter 1?
options: The son of David, king in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: The son of David, king in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:1 states that the words are of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What phrase does the Preacher repeat to describe the nature of all things?
questions.correctAnswer: Vanity of vanities
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:2 says, 'Vanity of vanities; all is vanity.'

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 1:3, what question does the Preacher ask about man's labor?
options: What profit hath a man of all his labour which he taketh under the sun?
How can a man rest after his labor?
questions.correctAnswer: What profit hath a man of all his labour which he taketh under the sun?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:3 asks, 'What profit hath a man of all his labour which he taketh under the sun?'

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 1:4 states that the earth changes with every generation.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:4 says 'One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh: but the earth abideth for ever.' This means the earth remains unchanged by generations.

questions.question: What natural phenomenon is described in Ecclesiastes 1:5?
options: The sun ariseth and goeth down, hastening to its place
The stars shine brightly at night
The rain falls from the clouds
questions.correctAnswer: The sun ariseth and goeth down, hastening to its place
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:5 says, 'The sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his place where he arose.'

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 1:6, which directions does the wind go toward and turn about to?
questions.correctAnswer: South and then north
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:6 describes the wind going toward the south and turning about unto the north.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 1:7 explains that rivers fill the sea until it overflows.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:7 says that all rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 1:8, which sense is said to never be satisfied?
questions.correctAnswer: The eye with seeing
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:8 says, 'the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.'

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 1:9 say about new things under the sun?
options: There is no new thing under the sun
Only the wise see new things
New things are found in the heavens
questions.correctAnswer: There is no new thing under the sun
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:9 states, 'there is no new thing under the sun.'

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 1:10 says some things may be new to us but existed before.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:10 says that what may seem new has already been before us in old times.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 1:11, what is said about the remembrance of former and future things?
options: There is no remembrance of former things or future things
Both former and future things are celebrated
questions.correctAnswer: There is no remembrance of former things or future things
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:11 states there is no remembrance of former things nor of future things with those who come after.

questions.question: Who was the Preacher king over Israel in Jerusalem, as stated in Ecclesiastes 1:12?
questions.correctAnswer: The Preacher himself
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:12 says, 'I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.'

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 1:13 says that God gave man the task of seeking wisdom.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:13 states that God has given to the sons of man the sore travail to seek and search out wisdom concerning all things done under heaven.

questions.question: Which statement comes first in Ecclesiastes 1:14-18?
options: All is vanity and vexation of spirit
That which is crooked cannot be made straight
I have more wisdom than those before me
questions.correctAnswer: All is vanity and vexation of spirit
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:14 is the first statement in the sequence, affirming that all work under the sun is vanity and vexation of spirit.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 1:15 say about things that are crooked or wanting?
options: That which is crooked cannot be made straight, and that which is wanting cannot be numbered
Crooked things can be fixed easily
That which is wanting can be fulfilled with effort
Crooked things are better than straight things
questions.correctAnswer: That which is crooked cannot be made straight, and that which is wanting cannot be numbered
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:15 states that crooked things cannot be made straight and things that are wanting cannot be numbered.

medium.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ecclesiastes Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 1:7, what happens to the rivers after they run into the sea?
options: They return to their original place
questions.correctAnswer: They return to their original place
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:7 states that all rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full, and the rivers return again to the place where they come from. This shows a continuous cycle of water movement.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 1:8 say about man's satisfaction with seeing and hearing?
options: The eye is satisfied with seeing, and the ear is filled with hearing
The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing
Only the ear is satisfied with hearing
Only the eye is satisfied with seeing
questions.correctAnswer: The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:8 explains that all things are full of labour and man cannot utter it; specifically, it says the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing, indicating human desires are never fully satisfied.

questions.question: What truth about novelty does Ecclesiastes 1:9 teach?
options: Everything under the sun is new and unique
There is no new thing under the sun
Only the wise recognize new things
questions.correctAnswer: There is no new thing under the sun
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:9 states that the thing that has been will be again, and there is no new thing under the sun, showing the repetitive nature of life and human experience.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 1:10 emphasize the concept of newness?
options: All new things are created by God
What is new has existed before us
New inventions are signs of progress
questions.correctAnswer: What is new has existed before us
questions.explanation: Verse 10 reiterates that anything considered new has already existed long ago before us, reinforcing the message in verse 9 about the absence of true novelty under the sun.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 1:11, what is said about the remembrance of past and future things?
options: Future things will be remembered by those who come after
There is no remembrance of former things nor of future things
Only the wise remember former things
questions.correctAnswer: There is no remembrance of former things nor of future things
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:11 points out that people forget past things and will also forget future things, emphasizing human forgetfulness and the fleeting nature of memory.

questions.question: Who identifies himself as the king over Israel in Jerusalem in Ecclesiastes 1:12?
questions.correctAnswer: The Preacher
questions.explanation: In Ecclesiastes 1:12, the speaker identifies himself as the Preacher who was king over Israel in Jerusalem, traditionally understood as Solomon, the son of David.

questions.question: What task did God give to the sons of man according to Ecclesiastes 1:13?
options: To seek and search out wisdom concerning all things
questions.correctAnswer: To seek and search out wisdom concerning all things
questions.explanation: Verse 13 illustrates that God gave humans the difficult task of seeking and searching out wisdom about all that is done under heaven, calling it a sore travail or hard labor.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 1:14 summarize the Preacher's observation about all works done under the sun?
options: All is vanity and vexation of spirit
questions.correctAnswer: All is vanity and vexation of spirit
questions.explanation: In verse 14, the Preacher reflects that after observing all works done under the sun, he finds them all to be vanity and vexation of spirit, emphasizing the futility and frustration in human endeavors.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 1:15 say about things that are crooked or wanting?
options: Crooked things can be made straight and wanting things can be numbered
Crooked things cannot be made straight and wanting things cannot be numbered
questions.correctAnswer: Crooked things cannot be made straight and wanting things cannot be numbered
questions.explanation: Verse 15 teaches that some things, like what is crooked, cannot be made straight, and what is lacking cannot be fully counted, highlighting the limitations of human ability to fix everything.

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 1:16, what does the Preacher say about his wisdom compared to others before him in Jerusalem?
options: He had less wisdom than others
He had equal wisdom to others
He had more wisdom than all who were before him
questions.correctAnswer: He had more wisdom than all who were before him
questions.explanation: Verse 16 reveals the Preacher's reflection that he had come to great estate and gained more wisdom than all who had been before him in Jerusalem, showing his pursuit and attainment of knowledge.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 1:17 say the Preacher sought to know, and what was his conclusion?
options: He sought to know health and wealth, and found them fulfilling
He sought to know wisdom, madness, and folly, and found them vexation of spirit
He sought only wisdom and found peace
questions.correctAnswer: He sought to know wisdom, madness, and folly, and found them vexation of spirit
questions.explanation: Verse 17 states that the Preacher gave his heart to know wisdom, madness, and folly, but concluded that even this pursuit brought vexation of spirit, emphasizing the frustration in human understanding.

questions.question: What relationship between wisdom and sorrow is taught in Ecclesiastes 1:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Much wisdom brings much grief
questions.explanation: Verse 18 teaches that with an increase in wisdom comes an increase in grief and sorrow, implying that greater understanding also reveals life's difficulties.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 1:9 declares that there is always something new and never before seen under the sun.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:9 explicitly states that there is no new thing under the sun, meaning nothing is truly new or never seen before.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ecclesiastes 1:11, people will remember the things that are to come with those who come after.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:11 says there is no remembrance of former things nor any remembrance of things to come with those who come after, highlighting human forgetfulness.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 1:8 indicates that human desires for seeing and hearing are never fully satisfied.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 8 explains that the eye is not satisfied with seeing and the ear is not filled with hearing, illustrating the insatiable nature of human desires.

hard.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ecclesiastes Chapter 1.

questions.question: What task has God given to the sons of man according to Ecclesiastes 1:13?
options: To seek and search out by wisdom all things done under heaven
To conquer the earth and subdue it
To multiply and fill the earth
questions.correctAnswer: To seek and search out by wisdom all things done under heaven
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:13 states that God has given the sons of man the sore travail to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all things done under heaven.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 1:14, what is the Preacher's conclusion after seeing all the works done under the sun?
options: All is vanity and vexation of spirit
questions.correctAnswer: All is vanity and vexation of spirit
questions.explanation: In Ecclesiastes 1:14, the Preacher concludes that all the works done under the sun are vanity and vexation of spirit.

questions.question: Ecclesiastes 1:15 uses the imagery of something crooked and something wanting. What does the verse say about these?
options: That which is crooked cannot be made straight; and that which is wanting cannot be numbered
That which is crooked can be straightened; and that which is wanting can be fulfilled
That which is crooked is good; and that which is wanting is evil
That which is crooked is hidden; and that which is wanting is seen
questions.correctAnswer: That which is crooked cannot be made straight; and that which is wanting cannot be numbered
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:15 teaches that some things are inherently crooked and cannot be made straight, and some things are wanting and cannot be numbered, illustrating the limitations of human effort.

questions.question: What does the Preacher say about his own wisdom and experience in Ecclesiastes 1:16?
options: He has more wisdom and knowledge than all before him in Jerusalem
He has less wisdom than the elders
He has no wisdom or knowledge
He relies only on the wisdom of others
questions.correctAnswer: He has more wisdom and knowledge than all before him in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:16 records the Preacher's reflection that he has attained great estate and more wisdom and knowledge than all who were before him in Jerusalem.

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 1:17, the Preacher sought to know wisdom and what else?
questions.correctAnswer: Madness and folly
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:17 shows the Preacher gave his heart to know wisdom as well as madness and folly, perceiving that all are vexation of spirit.

questions.question: What is the relationship between wisdom and grief according to Ecclesiastes 1:18?
options: In much wisdom is much grief; he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow
questions.correctAnswer: In much wisdom is much grief; he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:18 states that much wisdom results in much grief, and increasing knowledge leads to increasing sorrow.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme that 'there is no new thing under the sun' as stated in Ecclesiastes 1:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 90:9
questions.explanation: Psalm 90:9 speaks of generations coming and going, and human toil being consistent across time, echoing Ecclesiastes 1:9's theme of no new thing under the sun.

questions.question: The phrase 'vanity of vanities' in Ecclesiastes 1:2 is an example of which literary device commonly used in Hebrew poetry?
questions.correctAnswer: Intensification by repetition
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:2 uses repetition 'vanity of vanities' to intensify the concept, a common Hebrew poetic device.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'vanity' (hebel) imply in Ecclesiastes 1:2?
questions.correctAnswer: Vapor, breath, or something fleeting
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'hebel' means vapor or breath, implying something transient or meaningless as used in Ecclesiastes 1:2.

questions.question: Ecclesiastes 1:4 contrasts generations passing with what enduring element?
options: The rivers flow to the sea
questions.correctAnswer: The earth abideth forever
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:4 contrasts the passing of generations with the earth that remains forever.

questions.question: The cyclical nature of the sun described in Ecclesiastes 1:5 is an example of what broader theme in the chapter?
options: The repetitive and unchanging nature of life under the sun
The power of the sun god
questions.correctAnswer: The repetitive and unchanging nature of life under the sun
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:5 illustrates the sun's daily rising and setting as part of the chapter's theme of life's repetitive cycles.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the idea in Ecclesiastes 1:18 that increasing knowledge leads to sorrow?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Corinthians 8:1
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 8:1 warns that knowledge can puff up but love edifies, reflecting the caution in Ecclesiastes 1:18 about sorrow increasing with knowledge.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 1:11 teaches that future generations will remember the works and events of former times.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:11 states there is no remembrance of former things nor of things to come among future generations, making the statement false.

questions.question: True or False: The Preacher in Ecclesiastes 1 claims to be the son of David and king in Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:1 explicitly identifies the Preacher as the son of David, king in Jerusalem, affirming that the statement is true.

questions.question: Ecclesiastes 1:7 describes rivers running into the sea but the sea not being full. What broader concept does this illustrate in the chapter?
options: The endless cycles and futility of natural processes
The abundance of water on earth
The power of the sea god
questions.correctAnswer: The endless cycles and futility of natural processes
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:7 uses the image of rivers continually flowing into the sea without filling it to illustrate the endless and often futile cycles under the sun.

theological.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ecclesiastes Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What foundational truth about human labor is emphasized in Ecclesiastes 1:3?
options: Human labor under the sun is ultimately profitless
Human labor always leads to joy
questions.correctAnswer: Human labor under the sun is ultimately profitless
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:3 states, 'What profit hath a man of all his labour which he taketh under the sun?' emphasizing the vanity or futility of human labor apart from God.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is illustrated by the perpetual cycles of the sun and wind described in verses 5 and 6?
questions.correctAnswer: God's immutability
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:5-6 describe the sun rising and setting and the wind's continual circuits, reflecting God's unchanging, consistent governance of creation, revealing His immutability.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is highlighted by the statement in Ecclesiastes 1:9 that 'there is no new thing under the sun'?
options: Doctrine of God’s sovereignty over history
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of God’s sovereignty over history
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:9 underscores the repetitive nature of human experience, implying God's sovereign control over the unfolding of history where nothing is truly new, affirming divine providence.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 1:12-13, what has God given to the sons of man to be exercised with?
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom and travail
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:12-13 shows that God has given mankind the task to seek wisdom concerning all things under heaven, which is described as a 'sore travail' or painful labor.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 1:14 teach about the works done under the sun?
options: They are vanity and vexation of spirit
questions.correctAnswer: They are vanity and vexation of spirit
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:14 expresses the Preacher’s observation that all works under the sun are vanity (meaning emptiness) and vexation of spirit (meaning frustrating to the soul).

questions.question: What insight about human perception and satisfaction is given in Ecclesiastes 1:8?
options: The eye and ear are always satisfied
The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing
Man finds ultimate satisfaction in knowledge
Human senses are perfect and complete
questions.correctAnswer: The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:8 reveals the insatiable nature of human desire and perception, emphasizing that sensory satisfaction is never fully attained.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'the earth abideth for ever' in Ecclesiastes 1:4 teach about creation?
options: The earth is temporary like man
The earth is eternal and unchanging in its existence
The earth will be destroyed soon
The earth is subject to human control
questions.correctAnswer: The earth is eternal and unchanging in its existence
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:4 contrasts the fleeting nature of human generations with the enduring existence of the earth, teaching the permanence of creation as ordained by God.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 1:15 teach about the nature of certain realities in life?
options: All crooked things can be made straight
What is crooked cannot be made straight; and what is wanting cannot be numbered
All imperfections will be fixed by human effort
questions.correctAnswer: What is crooked cannot be made straight; and what is wanting cannot be numbered
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:15 teaches the intractable nature of some realities, highlighting human limitation and the persistence of imperfection in the fallen world.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 1:16-17 illustrate the relationship between wisdom and human experience?
options: Wisdom brings only joy and peace
Wisdom encompasses knowledge of madness and folly and brings vexation of spirit
Wisdom is irrelevant to human experience
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom encompasses knowledge of madness and folly and brings vexation of spirit
questions.explanation: Verses 16-17 show that the Preacher, despite his great wisdom, recognizes that knowing wisdom also involves knowing madness and folly, which causes vexation of spirit.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Ecclesiastes 1:17 and 1:18 convey about the pursuit of wisdom and knowledge?
options: Pursuit of wisdom leads to happiness
Pursuit of wisdom increases grief and sorrow
Pursuit of wisdom is easy and rewarding
questions.correctAnswer: Pursuit of wisdom increases grief and sorrow
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:17-18 together teach that increased wisdom and knowledge bring increased grief and sorrow, showing the paradoxical burden of understanding human limitations.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 1:11 relate to the doctrine of human memory and history?
options: Human memory preserves all past and future events
There is no remembrance of former things and future things will be forgotten also
History is fully reliable and permanent
questions.correctAnswer: There is no remembrance of former things and future things will be forgotten also
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:11 emphasizes the fleeting nature of human remembrance, implying a limitation in human history and memory, which contrasts with God’s eternal memory (Psalm 77:11-12).

questions.question: What apologetic response does Ecclesiastes 1:9-10 provide to the sceptic who claims that human history is full of novelty and progress?
options: History is entirely unpredictable and new
There is no new thing under the sun; all has been before
questions.correctAnswer: There is no new thing under the sun; all has been before
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:9-10 counters the sceptic’s claim by teaching that everything has been done before, revealing the cyclical and repetitive nature of human history under God’s sovereign plan.

questions.question: What does the description in Ecclesiastes 1:7 about rivers running into the sea and the sea not being full signify about creation?
options: Creation operates in a continual cyclical order
Creation is irrelevant to human life
questions.correctAnswer: Creation operates in a continual cyclical order
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:7 illustrates the cyclical nature of creation, showing the continual, ordered processes under God’s sustaining power.

questions.question: What doctrine is taught by the contrast between human generations passing and the earth abiding forever in Ecclesiastes 1:4?
options: Doctrine of creation’s permanence versus human mortality
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of creation’s permanence versus human mortality
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:4 contrasts the transient nature of human life with the enduring creation, teaching the doctrine that the created order remains while humans are mortal.

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by synthesizing Ecclesiastes 1:2 and 1:14 about the nature of human endeavors?
options: Human endeavors are ultimately meaningful and eternal
Human endeavors under the sun are vanity and vexation of spirit
Human endeavors are irrelevant to God
questions.correctAnswer: Human endeavors under the sun are vanity and vexation of spirit
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 1:2 and 1:14 both emphasize the vanity (emptiness) and vexation (frustration) involved in human works and labor under the sun, highlighting existential futility apart from God.
